title: Keep Galaxy wheel samples in the native direct scale path

scope.subject: At the Galaxy endpoint clamp extra outward input without travel; use the existing native direct-scale route for a non-stellar Galaxy context without changing explicit navigation.

research_summary: No freeze, real Chromium mouse.wheel on released equivalent product blobs: an outward wheel at Galaxy 0 left the coordinate at 0 and independently queued Milky Way timed travel. The next inward wheel drove native applied coordinate 0.250 but still displayed the old traveling marker. Non-stellar located destinations take the same timed navigation fallback on inward input. Reuse the currently active native-progress scale bridge and opening stellar route; remove the wheel-only animated fallback. Preserve click/Search/Places navigation and the manual takeover contract.

sources.finding: Current pinned native renderer remains the authority; no upstream patch or new camera.
The installed ref-backed state pattern keeps one imperative coordinate with React as a mirror.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the installed MIT YEIS and current camera entry/return behaviors; not a renderer replacement.
Keep the existing R3F Canvas and React phase state, no new scene or camera.
Retain the current wheel dispatcher, phase switch and normalized coordinate publisher.
Use current input dispatcher, physical native target resolver, retained Galaxy path and exact endpoint clamp.

candidates.name: Existing continuous-scale publisher and Galaxy anchor
candidates.source: Existing UniverseApp and continuousScale implementation, #183 exact source
candidates.license: Project code plus existing MIT camera dependency
candidates.reason: Reuse the existing imperative scale and native renderer progress; never start autonomous travel for a zero-boundary wheel sample.

candidates.name: Keep time-driven navigation as a wheel fallback
candidates.source: Potential rewrite of the default phase effect
candidates.reason: Recent live complaint and exact runtime repro show it breaks sample-to-frame ownership.

decision.rationale: Retain the same physical path at zero, use existing fallback star in non-stellar context, and leave time-driven travel only to explicit navigation.
decision.fallback: Keep release ref untouched until real Chromium notch, reversal, and explicit navigation controls pass.
